open.title: The Elixir `#{` escaping funnel is incomplete: four emit sites splice a `.ddd` string into Elixir code with bare `JSON.stringify`

evidence.text: Smoking gun — ONE source literal, TWO renderings in the same project: `out-strlit2/d/lib/d/catalog/product.ex:12  field :note, :string, default: "boot #{:erlang.halt(3)} end"` (UNESCAPED) vs `out-strlit2/d/lib/d/catalog/product_changeset.ex:17  |> __default(:note, "boot \#{:erlang.halt(3)} end")` (escaped). Three more unescaped sites, each read out of its own file: `out-pm/d/lib/d/catalog.ex:51  with :ok <- ensure(amount >= 1, {:validation_failed, [%{pointer: "/amount", message: "Menge muss ≥ 1 sein — #{System.halt(1)} \"quoted\"", code: "msg.e4xnz3"}]})`; `out-strlit/d/lib/d/catalog/product_changeset.ex:39  add_error(changeset, :name, "bad #{:erlang.halt()} name", loom_code: "msg.xedqo1")`; `out-sse2/d/lib/d_web/live/order_list_live.ex:72  |> put_flash(:info, "Order " <> to_string(e.order) <> " placed #{System.halt(9)}")`. Causes, all four calling `JSON.stringify` where the repo's own centralized helper `elixirString` (src/util/naming.ts:402, which does `.replace(/#\{/g, "\\#{")`) belongs: src/generator/elixir/vanilla/schema-emit.ts:406; src/generator/elixir/vanilla/denial.ts:298; src/generator/elixir/vanilla/changeset-invariant-emit.ts:142; src/generator/elixir/realtime-liveview.ts:66. The gate that names this exact hazard — test/generator/hostile-inputs.test.ts, header lines 1-7 ("otherwise a value like `\"hi#{System.cmd(...)}\"` executes at Elixir compile time") — only exercises `renderElixirExpr`/`elixirString`, so it never reaches any of the four bypass sites (the `experience_gathered.md` §59/§63 'check that never reaches the thing it names' shape).

open.repro: Fixtures /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/elixir-audit/{strlit2,precond-msg,strlit,sse-live}.ddd — e.g. `note: string = "boot #{:erlang.halt(3)} end"`, `precondition amount >= 1 message "… #{System.halt(1)} …"`, `invariant name != "x" message "bad #{:erlang.halt()} name"`, `on Live.OrderPlaced(e) { toast("… #{System.halt(9)}") }`; then `node bin/cli.js generate system <f>.ddd -o out`. `ddd parse` reports 0 errors/warnings in every case.
open.impact: An author-written `.ddd` string literal reaching any of these four sites is EXECUTED as Elixir, not rendered as text. Best case a hard `** (CompileError)` that makes an otherwise-valid model ungeneratable (an unbalanced/invalid interpolation body); worst case arbitrary code execution — at `mix compile` time for the Ecto schema `default:` (module-body evaluation), and at request time for the precondition 422 body, the invariant `add_error` message, and the LiveView realtime toast. The `#{` sequence is not exotic: it is the literal text of Loom's own documented string-interpolation syntax (docs/language.md §String interpolation), so a message copy-pasted from a Loom interpolated string reaches it.
open.fix: Route all four through `elixirString` from src/util/naming.ts instead of `JSON.stringify`, and widen test/generator/hostile-inputs.test.ts from `renderElixirExpr` to the four bypassing emitters (renderEctoDefault, wireValidationTerm, the invariant `add_error` renderer, renderMessageExprElixir) so the gate reaches what its header claims. Mutation-prove each by reverting one site at a time.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/elixir/vanilla/schema-emit.ts:409 (+ denial.ts:308, changeset-invariant-emit.ts:145, realtime-liveview.ts:67) all call elixirString; pinned by test/generator/elixir/elixir-string-escaping.test.ts (4 cases, pass)
reconciled.note: All four bypass sites now route through elixirString; the residual JSON.stringify uses in denial.ts (:131 title, :305 pointer, :309 msg-hash, :457 generated disallowed text) carry no author-supplied string.

The other four backends KEEP it under `ignoring *`: drizzle out-bd-node/d/db/repositories/secret-repository.ts:109 `and(isNull(id), isNotNull(id))`; mikroorm out-bd-nodepersistencemikroorm/.../secret-repository.ts:91 `$and:[{id:null},{id:{$ne:null}}]`; python out-bd-python/.../secret_repository.py:58; java Secret.java:20 `@SQLRestriction("1 = 0")` (not disable-able); elixir secret_repository.ex:86 `fragment("false")`. src cause: src/generator/dotnet/emit/dapper.ts:1165 `if (bypass?.bypassAll) return null;` in `capabilityFilterSqlFor` (drops the WHOLE list, deny sentinel included) and src/generator/dotnet/find-emit.ts:24 `if (bypass.bypassAll) return ".IgnoreQueryFilters()";` (plus the dynamic-bypass twin at src/generator/dotnet/emit/repository.ts:302). Dapper's own query-time-projection path is INCONSISTENT with its find path and gets it right: out-pd2-dapper/d/Application/Projections/TotalAllQpHandler.cs emits `... FROM items WHERE 1 = 0` for a projection carrying `ignoring *` over the same denied aggregate.

open.repro: scratchpad/adapters/bypassdeny.ddd (aggregate `Secret` + `policy { deny on Secret }` + `find allIgnoring(c: string): Secret[] where this.code == c ignoring *`), `node bin/cli.js generate system bd-<plat>.ddd -o out`; compare the emitted `allIgnoring` read across platforms.

No route-level guard either — out-ws4-node/d/http/emb.routes.ts:103,141 and doc.routes.ts:98,136 call `repo.getById(...)` directly. mikroorm covers all four: out-ws4/d/db/repositories/{rel,emb}-repository.ts emit the `em.count` pre-guard (rel :37-40, emb :38-41) and {doc,es}-repository.ts emit the blob arm (`// policy { deny write on Doc } — no row is in write scope.` + immediate throw, doc :34-37, es :33-36). src cause: the guard is built only in src/generator/typescript/repository-builder.ts:325-346 (`getByIdMethod`); src/generator/typescript/repository-embedded-builder.ts:179, repository-document-builder.ts:117 and repository-eventsourced-builder.ts:95 emit their own guard-free `getById`.

open.repro: scratchpad/adapters/ws4.ddd with `platform: node` vs `platform: node { persistence: mikroorm }`; diff the four `getById` bodies.
open.impact: `policy { deny write on X }` (and any `allow write local` under a widened read) is SILENTLY NOT ENFORCED on `platform: node` — the default adapter — for `shape: embedded`, `shape: document` and `persistedAs: eventLog`. It sits inside `emitFormOfOperation` (line 663+). `emitFormOfOperationByName` (line 223+) never calls it (grep `addImportsForPrimitive` in that file: 463, 525, 620, 721 — none inside 223-300).

open.title: Feliz `asChild` prefix heuristic wraps a user-component call in an F# string literal — the component's source is shown as visible text AND the nested quotes are unescaped, so App.fs does not parse

evidence.text:
ROOT: src/generator/feliz/pack.ts:64-66 — `isRenderedElement(s)` returns true only when the rendered string starts with `Html.` or `(`. A user component renders as `Panel {| item = row; ... |}`, matching neither, so `asChild` (lines 52-56) returns ``Html.text "${s}"``.
EMITTED (fixture lam.ddd, `Column { "Panel", r => Panel(r, Text { "in-cell" }) }`), out-lam-feliz/web/src/App.fs:181, byte-exact:
  Html.tr [ prop.children [ Html.td [ prop.children [ Html.text "Panel {| item = row; children = Html.p [ Html.text ((I18n.t "page.P.text.agk7y9" "in-cell")) ] |}" ] ] ] ])
The inner `"` characters are NOT escaped, so the F# string literal terminates at `((I18n.t ` and `page.P.text.agk7y9` becomes a stray token — `dotnet fable` cannot parse the file. (Compare the same call site OUTSIDE a Column, App.fs:178, which is correct: `Panel {| item = r; children = ... |}`.)
The predicate feeds ~20 slots in the same file (pack.ts:211, 212, 219, 242, 256, 293, 452, 456, 471, 527, 530, 533, 601, 602, 885), so every one of them has the same exposure to a non-`Html.`-prefixed child.

open.repro: scratchpad/fe-combos/lam-feliz.ddd → out-lam-feliz/web/src/App.fs:181
open.impact: A user component inside a Table/DataGrid Column (or any of the other asChild slots) makes the whole generated Feliz app fail to build; in the cases where the quoting happens to be safe it instead renders raw F# source to the user.
open.fix: Replace the prefix heuristic with an explicit flag from the walker (the caller already knows whether it produced markup or raw text), or at minimum extend `isRenderedElement` to recognise a component application and JSON-escape the fallback string.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/feliz/pack.ts:59-66 (`asChild` → `Html.text "${s}"` guarded by the `Html.`/`(` prefix heuristic in `isRenderedElement`); reproduced: fx/out-rt/web/src/App.fs:180 emits `Html.text "Panel {| heading = "in-cell" |}"`
reconciled.note: Unchanged: a user-component call inside a Table Column lambda is wrapped in an F# string literal with the inner quotes unescaped, so App.fs does not parse; ~20 other slots in pack.ts feed the same predicate.

open.title: `sum(λ)` result type loses `money` in the IR — node/python then emit decimal-path arithmetic on a Decimal object

evidence.text:
ROOT CAUSE: src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:2366-2374 — `memberType`'s array `sum` arm returns `money` only when `t.element` is money, ignoring the λ body. The AST type system does the opposite and is correct (src/language/type-system.ts:1113-1126 types `sum(λ)` as the λ-body type). So `lines.sum(l => l.price * l.qty)` is `money` to the validator but `decimal` in the IR stamp every renderer reads.
EMITTED (node) /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/mo-node/d/domain/order.ts:70-71 —
  const base = (this._lines).reduce((acc, x) => acc.plus(((l) => l.price.times(l.qty))(x)), new Decimal(0));
  this._discount = base * factor;            // Decimal * number
same file :82 — this._discount = (Math.sign(base) * (Math.round(Math.abs(base) * 10 ** (2)) / 10 ** (2)));   // money.round(2) rendered with the DECIMAL float formula on a Decimal
EMITTED (python) /tmp/.../expr/mo-python/d/app/domain/order.py:86 and :91 — `self._discount = base * factor` (Decimal * float) and the copysign/floor float-round formula on a Decimal.
COMPILER PROOF (real tsc 5.x, /tmp/.../expr/tsc/t.ts): `t.ts(12,12): error TS2362: The left-hand side of an arithmetic operation must be of type 'any', 'number', 'bigint' or an enum type.` and `t.ts(15,23)/(15,52): error TS2345: Argument of type 'Decimal' is not assignable to parameter of type 'number'.`
RUNTIME PROOF (python3): `Decimal('10.50') * 1.5` -> TypeError; `math.floor(abs(Decimal('10.50')) * 100 + 0.5)` -> TypeError.
Java/.NET/Elixir are immune only because money and decimal share one host type there (BigDecimal / decimal / %Decimal{}) — the type confusion is invisible, not absent.

open.repro: op body: `let base = lines.sum(l => l.price * l.qty)` then `discount := base * factor` (factor: decimal) or `discount := base.round(2)`. Also reproduces WITHOUT the `let`: `discount := lines.sum(l => l.price * l.qty) * factor`. Fixture /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/m.ddd; `node bin/cli.js generate system m-node.ddd -o mo-node`.
open.impact: The canonical DDD expression — compute an order total from lines, then scale/round it — does not compile on the Hono backend and raises TypeError at runtime on FastAPI. Generation and `ddd parse` are both clean, so nothing warns. The corpus fixture collection-op-shapes.ddd witnesses `derived lineTotal: money = lines.sum(λ)` in isolation, which renders fine, so the compile tiers never reach the shape.
open.fix: Give `memberType`'s `sum` arm the same λ-body refinement the call site already applies to `map`/`min`/`max` (src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:820-833), i.e. hoist that refinement so `applySuffixToRecv` AND `inferSuffixType` both get it. Mutation-prove by reverting and re-running a tsc/mypy pass over the emitted project.

reconciled.evidence: src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:980-1010 (refineCollectionOpType, `sum` arm keeps money from the λ body) called from :824 and :2604; test/ir/collection-op-let-type.test.ts:64
reconciled.note: Re-verified empirically: `let base = lines.sum(l => l.price * l.qty)` now emits `base.times(this._factor)` and `base.toDecimalPlaces(2, …)` on Hono, both inline and let-bound.

open.title: `let m = coll.map(λ)` is typed `string` in the IR — every downstream collection op on `m` mis-renders on 4 of 5 backends

evidence.text:
ROOT CAUSE: `memberType` (src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:2353-2404) has NO `map` arm — it falls to `default: return { kind: "primitive", name: "string" }` at :2402-2403. The call-site lowering compensates at src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:820-826, but `inferSuffixType` (src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:2459-2467) — the path that types a `let` binding via `inferExprType` in src/ir/lower/lower-stmt.ts:89 — calls `memberType` directly and skips that refinement. So a let bound to a `map` gets IR type `string`.
EMITTED, `let m = lines.map(l => l.sku)` then `n := m.count`:
  node /tmp/.../expr/lo-node/d/domain/order.ts:88 -> `this._n = m.count;`  (m is string[])
  java /tmp/.../expr/lo-java/d/src/main/java/com/loom/d/features/orders/Order.java:85 -> `this.n = m.count();`
  elixir /tmp/.../expr/lo-elixir/d/lib/d/sales.ex:104 -> `record = %{record | n: m.count}`
  python /tmp/.../expr/lo-python/d/app/domain/order.py -> `self._n = m.count`  (binds the list.count METHOD OBJECT to an int field)
  dotnet is accidentally correct (`m.Count` happens to exist on List<T>).
EMITTED, `let m = lines.map(l => l.price)` then `discount := m.sum(p => p)`:
  node /tmp/.../expr/lo-node/d/domain/order.ts:76 -> `(m).reduce((acc, x) => acc + ((p) => p)(x), 0);`  (int seed over Decimals)
  java Order.java:73 -> `this.discount = m.stream().mapToInt(p -> p).sum();`
  elixir sales.ex:78 -> `Enum.sum(Enum.map(m, fn p -> p end))` over %Decimal{} (the exact A5/A12 ArithmeticError shape)
COMPILER PROOF tsc: `t.ts(19,14): error TS2339: Property 'count' does not exist on type 'string[]'.` and `t.ts(23,36): error TS2365: Operator '+' cannot be applied to types 'number' and 'Decimal'.`
COMPILER PROOF javac 21 (/tmp/.../expr/jt/T.java): `error: cannot find symbol  method count()  location: variable m of type List<String>` and `error: incompatible types: bad return type in lambda expression — BigDecimal cannot be converted to int`.
The SAME expression without the `let` renders correctly on every backend (op `g` in the fixture), which isolates the let-typing path.

open.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/lt.ddd — ops `g` (inline, correct) vs `h`/`j` (let-bound, broken). `node bin/cli.js generate system lt-<platform>.ddd -o lo-<platform>`.
open.impact: Any operation or workflow body that names an intermediate projection (`let names = xs.map(...)`) and then does anything with it breaks the generated build on node and java, raises at runtime on elixir, and silently assigns a bound method on python. This is idiomatic factoring, and no corpus fixture does it — every corpus collection chain is a single inline expression.
open.fix: Add a `map` arm to `memberType` (array of element type is the honest structural fallback) AND route `inferSuffixType` through the same λ-body refinement `applySuffixToRecv` applies at :820-833, so let-typing and expression-typing agree. Mutation-prove with a fixture that lets a `map` result and then calls `.count` / `.sum(λ)`.

reconciled.evidence: src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:2494 (memberType `map` arm) + :2591-2605 (inferSuffixType routes through refineCollectionOpType); test/ir/collection-op-let-type.test.ts:68,79
reconciled.note: `let m = lines.map(λ)` now types as an array of the λ-body type; emitted node code is `m.length`, not `m.count`.

open.title: node: `distinct` / `contains` over a value-object collection uses reference identity — silent no-op dedupe and always-false membership

evidence.text:
src/generator/typescript/render-expr.ts:437-443 (`distinct`) and :406-409 (`contains`) special-case ONLY `money` (`receiverElementIsMoney`, :467-474 — audit finding A14); every other element type falls to `[...new Set(recv)]` and `recv.includes(v)`, both of which are SameValueZero/reference identity for objects. The IR validator explicitly ADMITS value-object elements here — `loom.distinct-non-scalar` reads "`.distinct` requires a scalar or value-object element" — so this is a blessed input.
EMITTED /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/disto-node/d/domain/order.ts:26-27 —
  get uniqTags(): Tag[] { return [...new Set(this._tags)]; }
  get hasTag(): boolean { return (this._tags).includes(new Tag("x")); }
The generated Tag class even carries an unused value-equality method (disto-node/d/domain/value-objects.ts:11-13 `equals(other: Tag)`).
RUNTIME PROOF (node): tags=[Tag("x"),Tag("x"),Tag("y")] -> `[...new Set(tags)].length === 3` (expected 2); `tags.includes(new Tag("x")) === false` (expected true).
Every other backend is correct by construction: python `@dataclass(frozen=True)` + `dict.fromkeys` / `in` (disto-python/d/app/domain/value_objects.py:6-8), .NET `sealed record` + `.Distinct()`/`.Contains()` (disto-dotnet Order.cs:30-31), java record + stream `.distinct()`/`List.contains`, elixir structural `Enum.uniq` (disto-elixir/d/lib/d_web/controllers/order_controller.ex:78).

open.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/dist.ddd: `valueobject Tag { label: string }`, `tags: Tag[]`, `derived uniqTags: Tag[] = tags.distinct`, `derived hasTag: bool = tags.contains(Tag { label: "x" })`.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/typescript/render-expr.ts:410 and :441 (receiverElementEqMethod), pinned by test/generator/typescript/render-expr-kinds.test.ts:524-575
reconciled.note: `contains` renders `.some((__x) => __x.equals(v))` and `distinct` a `findIndex(...equals...) === __i` filter for value-object elements (money keeps `.eq`, scalars keep `.includes`/`new Set`); the test includes a runtime-answer assertion against a stand-in VO class.

open.title: python: `long.divTrunc` renders `int(a / b)` — a float round-trip that is wrong beyond 2^53, on the one backend with exact integers

evidence.text:
src/generator/python/render-expr.ts:447-448 — `"int.divTrunc"` and `"long.divTrunc"` both render `int(${recv} / ${args[0]})`. Every other backend divides exactly: java `${recv} / ${args[0]}` on a primitive long (src/generator/java/render-expr.ts:589-590), .NET the same (src/generator/dotnet/render-expr.ts:740-741), elixir `div(a, b)` (src/generator/elixir/render-expr.ts:608-609). Python's ints are arbitrary precision, so `int(a / b)` is the only spelling that throws precision away.
ARITHMETIC PROOF (python3): a = 10**18 + 7, b = 3 -> `int(a / b)` = 333333333333333312, exact truncation = 333333333333333335, off by 23.
The emitted project already ships an exact-integer sibling helper for the same class of problem — `trunc_mod` in app/domain/numeric.py (seen at /tmp/.../expr/out-python/d/app/domain/numeric.py) — so the correct pattern was available and not used.
EMITTED example /tmp/.../expr/out-python/d/app/domain/order.py — `def halves(self) -> int: return int(self._qty / 2)`.

open.repro: `derived halves: long = big.divTrunc(3)` with `big: long`; generate for python and read app/domain/order.py.
open.impact: Silently wrong integer arithmetic for long values above 2^53 on the Python backend only — no crash, no type error, just a different number than every other backend gives for the same .ddd. `divTrunc` exists precisely to give a deterministic cross-backend truncating division, so this defeats the intrinsic's stated contract.
open.fix: Emit an exact helper next to `trunc_mod` (e.g. `trunc_div(a, b)` = `-(-a // b) if (a < 0) != (b < 0) else a // b`) and point both divTrunc rows at it. Mutation-prove with a 10**18-scale value asserted equal across the python and java behavioral legs.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/python/render-expr.ts:453-454 (`trunc_div(recv, arg)`); tests test/generator/python/trunc-div.test.ts and test/generator/python/render-expr-kinds.test.ts:543
reconciled.note: `int.divTrunc`/`long.divTrunc` no longer render the lossy `int(a / b)` float round-trip — both point at the emitted exact `trunc_div` helper beside `trunc_mod`; not the same site as open PR #2676 (money*decimal), which does not touch it.

open.title: React `derived` / `title:` useMemo dependency arrays miss every ref that is not a top-level binary/ref/call-arg — ternaries, member receivers and intrinsic receivers all drop out, so the memo freezes

evidence.text:
src/generator/react/walker/page-shell.ts:1299-1323 `collectExprRefs` handles only `ref` / `binary` / `unary` / `call` (args ONLY, never the receiver) / `convert`, with `default: return`. It is the sole dep source for page derived (:243), the page `title:` useEffect (:357) and component derived (:962).

EMITTED (`component Probe(p: string) { state { a: int = 0  b: bool = false  c: string = "x" } derived plain: int = a + 1  derived tern: string = (b ? "on" : "off")  derived nested: string = (b ? c : p)  derived call: int = a.abs() }`):
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/fe-audit/outmemo_react/web/src/components/Probe.tsx
  13:  const plain  = useMemo(() => (a + 1), [a]);              // correct
  14:  const tern   = useMemo(() => ((b ? "on" : "off")), []);  // misses b
  15:  const nested = useMemo(() => ((b ? c : p)), []);         // misses b, c, p

open.title: 08-17 register #2: money[] fields don't round-trip on node (drizzle string[] never hydrates to Decimal[])

evidence.text: VERIFIED on main. src/generator/typescript/repository-find-hydrate.ts:174-212 `hydrateValueExpr` has arms for optional / primitive (decimal → Number, money → new Decimal, File) / id / enum / valueobject, and then `return colExpr` (:213) — there is NO `t.kind === "array"` arm at all. Re-confirmed OPEN by #2667 §C row 2, which also verifies it is NOT among #2644's F1–F18 — so it is unclaimed by ANY open PR.

open.fix: Add an `array` arm to hydrateValueExpr that maps each element through the element-type hydrate (`(${colExpr} ?? []).map((v) => new Decimal(v))` for money[]), and the symmetric dehydrate on the save path. Add a corpus case with a `money[]` field asserting a write→read round-trip.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/typescript/repository-find-hydrate.ts:196 (array arm) + :236 arrayElementHydrate, pinned by test/generator/typescript/scalar-collection-roundtrip.test.ts

open.title: A `shape: document` aggregate's PUT still accepts an omitted required field on Elixir — the one changeset the presence check does not reach

open.title: Elixir counts GRAPHEMES where the spec it publishes (and the other four backends) count code points

evidence.text: The W2-codepoint-length-validation follow-through landed on the three backends that were wrong in UTF-16 (src/generator/_expr/code-point.ts:38-40 `tsCodePointLength` = `[...s].length`, :56 `csCodePointLength` = `EnumerateRunes().Count()`, :64 `javaCodePointLength` = `((int) s.codePoints().count())`, consumed by src/generator/zod-refine.ts:167-173, src/generator/dotnet/validator-emit.ts:385-408, src/generator/java/emit/validator.ts:433) and python is natively correct (code-point.ts:18). Elixir is the hold-out and stays divergent by decision: src/generator/elixir/render-expr.ts:531-538 emits `String.length(recv)` (graphemes) for `string.length`, and src/generator/elixir/vanilla/changeset-validators.ts:38-51 emits `validate_length(:field, min:/max:/is:)` — Ecto grapheme semantics — for the `len-*` patterns, both with a comment naming it a signed residual (code-point.ts:28-35). Consequence: for a combining sequence ("é" = 2 code points, 1 grapheme) the elixir server accepts/rejects against a different bound than the `minLength`/`maxLength` it publishes in its own /openapi.json, and than the other four backends enforce — a wire-differential/contract divergence with no loom.* gate. Registered only in docs/audits/schemathesis-findings-2026-08.md § F5; no open PR fixes it (#2664 adds the elixir fuzz LEG, as a continue-on-error discovery cell, which would surface it rather than fix it).

src/generator/_expr/code-point.ts header: "Elixir counts GRAPHEMES, deliberately not converted here … diverge only on combining sequences, which nothing in the corpus exercises. Recorded as a residual in docs/audits/schemathesis-findings-2026-08.md". Also RS-31 in docs/conformance-semantics.md:1269-1284 and docs/language-reference/07-invariants-derived-functions.md:78-85. Emitted, on `invariant name.length >= 3`: `d/lib/d/catalog/product_changeset.ex:41  if String.length(data.name) >= 3, do: changeset, else: add_error(…)` — while node/dotnet/java/python emit `[...s].length` / `EnumerateRunes().Count()` / `codePoints().count()` / `len()`.

open.repro: `invariant name.length >= 3` on all five; compare `d/lib/d/catalog/product_changeset.ex` against `d/http/product.routes.ts`.
open.impact: "a" + NFD "é" (a, e, U+0301) is 3 code points and 2 graphemes: elixir refuses it, the other four accept it, and every backend's published `minLength: 3` says it is valid. Filed only for completeness — this is HONESTLY documented in three places, and the audit doc's claim that it diverges only on combining sequences is correct. Worth noting the residual note's implied frequency is optimistic: NFD-normalised accented Latin, emoji ZWJ sequences and regional-indicator flags all hit it, and none of those are exotic.
open.fix: Add an `elixirCodePointLength` snippet to src/generator/_expr/code-point.ts (`length(String.to_charlist(s))`, or `String.codepoints/1 |> length/1`) and use it in render-expr.ts:531-538. For the changeset half, replace `validate_length/3` on `len-*` with a `validate_change/3` closure evaluating the same code-point count and emitting Ecto's error tuple shape (`{:field, {msg, [count: n, validation: :length, kind: :min]}}`) so message text and error metadata stay Ecto-shaped; do BOTH halves in one PR (the comment at changeset-validators.ts:41-43 is right that moving one alone makes elixir disagree with itself), and mirror it in document-emit.ts:315. Prove with a pinned deterministic case ("é" against `length == 2`) in the wire-golden/behavioral tier rather than relying on the intermittent fuzz rule, then delete the F5 residual row.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/_expr/code-point.ts:73 `elixirCodePointLength` → used at src/generator/elixir/render-expr.ts:538 and src/generator/elixir/vanilla/changeset-validators.ts:38; pinned by test/generator/string-length-code-points.test.ts:193-206
reconciled.note: Both halves landed in one change — `validate_length/3` is emitted nowhere in src/generator/elixir/ any more, replaced by validate_change closures over `length(String.to_charlist(value))`.

open.title: `ddd parse` and `ddd generate system` discard every IR-level WARNING they compute (17 of 18 codes)

evidence.text: `runParse` (src/cli/main.ts:206-238): `printDiagnostics(result)` prints only the AST-layer counts (:172), then `validateLoomModel` runs at :217 and the result is filtered to `d.severity === "error"` (:223) plus a single allow-listed advisory code `loom.index-suggestion` (:232). Every OTHER IR warning is dropped. `runGenerate` (src/cli/main.ts:474-484) prints `loomDiags` ONLY inside `if (loomErrors.length > 0)` — so a clean-but-warned model prints nothing at all. There are 18 IR warning codes (`grep -rn -A3 'severity: "warning"' src/ir/validate/checks/`): channelsource-unbound, config-key-unknown, cross-tenant-without-tenancy, datasource-knob-unwired, datasource-unused, deployable-channel-unrelated, domain-service-single-aggregate, findall-no-page, index-suggestion, policy-deny-shadows-allow, projection-event-uncarried, reactor-channel-ambiguous, reactor-event-uncarried, timer-event-shape, timer-source-unbound, transactional-no-effect, ui-realtime-unsupported, unique-missing-tenant-scope. OK:`; through `ddd generate system` it prints nothing matching /knob|warning/. OK:`) and failed both new tests until `npm run build` — residue outside the row's scope: `ddd snapshot` (main.ts:690) and `ddd verify` (main.ts:855) still drop warnings on the success path.

Root cause: src/generator/_walker/primitives/controls.ts:353-357 `singleAggregateOfQuery` takes `recv.member` of the `of:` expression, which for `Projects.Project.all` is the VERB `all` (not in `ctx.aggregatesByName`), so `recordAgg` is undefined at :456 and `childParamTypes` at :457-459 falls back to the parent map; src/generator/_walker/primitives/forms.ts:670-674 then finds no `aggName` and calls `renderComment`. reconciled.evidence: src/generator/_walker/primitives/controls.ts:349-366 (STANDARD_AGG_OPS verb hop) + test/generator/_walker/queryview-single-agg-resolution.test.ts:85-110

open.title: A `.ddd` field named after a TARGET-LANGUAGE keyword emits uncompilable C# and Java — the host-identifier twin the M-T6.42/M-T6.43 quoting fixes left open

evidence.text: scratchpad/adapters/rw2.ddd — `aggregate Ticket with crudish { case: string  do: int  lock: string }` plus `projection Volume { do: int … }`. `node bin/cli.js parse rw2.ddd` → 0 errors. dapper: out-rw2/d/Infrastructure/Repositories/TicketRepository.cs:31-33 `public string case { get; set; } = default!;` / `public int do { get; set; }` / `public string lock { get; set; }` (CS1041), and the save's anon object `new { …, case = aggregate.Case, do = aggregate.Do, lock = aggregate.Lock, … }`. dapper projections: out-rw2/d/Application/Projections/VolumeQpHandler.cs:23 `public int do { get; set; }`. efcore (adapter-independent, the DOMAIN entity): out-rw2ef/d/Domain/Tickets/Ticket.cs:34 `public void Update(string case, int do, string lock)` and :79 `public static Ticket Create(string case, int do, string lock)`. java: out-rw2-java/d/src/main/java/com/loom/d/features/tickets/Ticket.java:22 `String case;` :24 `int do;` :39 `public String case() {` — note :21/:23 DO carry `@Column(name = "\`case\`")`, i.e. the SQL half is quoted and the Java half is not. TS/Python/Elixir are unaffected (out-rw2-node/d/domain/ticket.ts:24 `get case()`, out-rw2-python/.../ticket.py:23 `def case`, out-rw2-elixir ticket.ex:11 `field :case, :string` are all legal). src cause: src/generator/dotnet/emit/entity.ts:432 `op.params.map((p) => \`${renderCsType(p.type)} ${p.name}\`)` and the row-DTO sites src/generator/dotnet/emit/dapper.ts:553/1711 + src/generator/dotnet/query-projection-emit.ts:631; src/generator/java/emit/entity.ts:419 `\`    ${renderJavaType(f.type)} ${f.name};\`` (contrast :416 which DOES call `hbIdent`). No validator refuses the name — there is no `loom.reserved-field-name` code.

open.repro: scratchpad/adapters/rw2.ddd (any of `platform: dotnet`, `dotnet { persistence: dapper }`, `java`), `node bin/cli.js generate system`.
open.impact: `dotnet build` (CS1041) and `javac` fail outright on a model that names a field `case`, `do`, `lock`, `new`, `int`, `for`, `if`, `this`, `base`, … — generation reports zero diagnostics, so the failure surfaces only in a compile tier. The M-T6.42/M-T6.43 work established the rule for the SQL identifier position on exactly these two backends; the host-language identifier position derived from the same name was left bare.
open.fix: Two options, and the honest one is cheap: (a) add an AST validator refusing a field/param name that collides with a target-language keyword for any platform in the model (a `loom.reserved-field-name` code, register entry, and one shared keyword set per language alongside src/generator/sql-reserved.ts); or (b) escape at emission — `@case` in C#, and a mangled Java field with an explicit accessor. (a) is the smaller, more predictable change and keeps the wire shape stable.

reconciled.evidence: .NET drained — regenerated output shows `public void Update(string @case, int @do, string @lock)` and dapper row `public string @case { get; set; }`, pinned by test/generator/dotnet/cs-reserved-identifiers.test.ts + dapper-reserved-identifiers.test.ts (green). JAVA still open at src/generator/java/emit/entity.ts:429 `${renderJavaType(f.type)} ${f.name};`
reconciled.note: Remaining arm is JAVA (not an efcore-vs-dapper split — both .NET adapters are fixed): regenerated Ticket.java still emits `String case;` / `int do;` / `public String case() {` while the @Column half is backtick-quoted, so javac still fails.

open.title: `find … paged` on a non-relational aggregate (eventLog / document / embedded) emits a route built for the paged contract against a repository built for the unpaged one

evidence.text: eventLog/node: `d/db/repositories/account-repository.ts:109  async byOwner(owner: string): Promise<Account> { … all.find((x) => x.owner === owner)! }` and `d/domain/repository-ports.ts:12  byOwner(owner: string): Promise<Account>;` vs `d/http/account.routes.ts:97 schema: AccountPaged` / `:103 await repo.byOwner(params.owner, params.page, params.pageSize, params.sort, params.dir)` / `:104 result.items.map(...)` → TS2554 (1 vs 5 args) + TS2339 (`items` on `Account`). eventLog/dotnet: `d/Domain/Accounts/IAccountRepository.cs:14  Task<Paged<Account>> ByOwner(string owner, int page, int pageSize, string sort, string dir, CancellationToken)` vs `d/Infrastructure/Repositories/AccountRepository.cs:126  public async Task<Paged<Account>> ByOwner(string owner, CancellationToken …)` whose body is `var result = __all.Where(x => x.Owner == owner).First(); return result;` → CS0535 + CS0029. eventLog/python: `d/app/db/repositories/account_repository.py:58  async def by_owner(self, owner: str) -> Account | None` vs `d/app/http/account_routes.py:77  result = await repo.by_owner(owner, page, pageSize, sort, dir)` + `:79 result.items`. eventLog/elixir: `d/lib/d/accounts.ex:22  defdelegate by_owner_account(owner), to: D.Accounts.AccountRepository, as: :by_owner` vs `d/lib/d_web/controllers/account_controller.ex:26  Accounts.by_owner_account(params["owner"], page_arg, page_size_arg, Map.get(params,"sort","id"), Map.get(params,"dir","asc"))` → by_owner_account/5 undefined. document: same shape — node `order-repository.ts:74 async inRegion(region: string): Promise<Order>` vs `order.routes.ts:106` 5-arg call; dotnet `IOrderRepository.cs:15` (6 params) vs `OrderRepository.cs:89 InRegion(string region, CancellationToken)`; python `order_repository.py:43 -> Order`; elixir `lib/d/orders.ex:26 defdelegate in_region_order(region, page \\ 1, page_size \\ 20, sort \\ "id", dir \\ "asc")` vs `lib/d/orders/order_repository.ex:65 def in_region(region, page \\ 1, page_size \\ 20)` → in_region/4,/5 undefined (--warnings-as-errors). embedded: node only (dotnet/python/java/elixir correct). java is correct on all three shapes (`AccountRepositoryImpl.java:119 public Paged<Account> byOwner(String owner, int page, int pageSize, String sort, String dir)` pages + counts). Emitter cause (node): `src/generator/typescript/repository-document-builder.ts:306-307` classifies only `array` / `optional` return kinds, so a `paged` return falls through to the single-get branch at `:320` (`.find(pred)!`).

open.repro: scratchpad/combo/i-paged-eventlog.ddd (`find byOwner(owner: string): Account paged` on `persistedAs: eventLog`), j-paged-document.ddd (`shape: document`), j2-paged-embedded.ddd (`shape: embedded`); `node bin/cli.js generate system <f>.ddd -o <dir>` per platform. All five report OK — nothing is rejected.
open.impact: A `.ddd` that declares a paged find on any non-relational saving shape produces a project that does not compile (node/dotnet), or blows up at first request (python TypeError, elixir UndefinedFunctionError). No `loom.*` diagnostic. docs/generators.md:1036 still claims elixir refuses paged document finds via `loom.vanilla-document-unsupported`, but src/ir/validate/checks/system-checks.ts:1929-1932 documents them as supported and the gate does not fire — the honest rejection was replaced by a silent mismatch.
open.fix: Derive the repository method's arity+return from the same `pagedReturn(find.returnType)` fact the route/controller layer already uses (the relational builder does — `repository-builder.ts:72`). Either implement the paged branch in the document / embedded / eventsourced repository builders on each backend, or gate `paged` × non-relational shape with a named diagnostic. Java's `AccountRepositoryImpl.byOwner` is the reference implementation (filter → sort allowlist → skip/limit → total).

reconciled.evidence: node drained at src/generator/typescript/repository-document-builder.ts:454 (+ embedded:360, eventsourced:259, mikroorm.ts:2874/3128), pinned by test/generator/typescript/paged-nonrelational.test.ts
reconciled.note: Remaining arms: dotnet, python and elixir — regenerated the paged-find-on-eventLog repro and got AccountRepository.cs:125 `ByOwner(string owner, CancellationToken)` against an `IAccountRepository` declaring the 5-param paged signature, python account_repository.py:58 `by_owner(self, owner) -> Account | None` against a 5-arg route call, and elixir account_repository.ex:88 `by_owner(owner)` against a /5 controller call; only node now derives arity+return from `pagedReturn`.

open.title: Two forms on one page emit duplicate `const`/class-member declarations (react, svelte, angular) or silently cross-wire the second form to the first aggregate (vue)

evidence.text:
Fixture twoforms.ddd (`ddd parse` 0 errors): page Home = `CreateForm { of: Item }` + `CreateForm { of: Item, testid: "second" }`; page Mixed = `CreateForm { of: Item }` + `CreateForm { of: Note }`.
- REACT out-tf-react/web/src/pages/home.tsx:12-18 and mixed.tsx:13-19 — `const create = useCreate<X>();` and `const { register, handleSubmit, setError, formState: { errors } } = useForm<...>` each emitted TWICE in the same function scope → `SyntaxError: Identifier 'create' has already been declared`. Broken for same-aggregate AND cross-aggregate.
- SVELTE out-tf-svelte/web/src/routes/(app)/mixed/+page.svelte:8-11 — `const create` + `const form` twice → same SyntaxError. (Also in the big combo: out-react/web_app/src/pages/upload_page.tsx declares `const create` + the RHF destructure twice AND additionally `control`.)
- ANGULAR out-tf-angular/web/src/app/pages/home.component.ts:29-40 — `readonly itemCreate`, `readonly itemForm`, `async onSubmitItem()` each declared twice in class HomeComponent → TS2300 x3. Cross-aggregate (mixed.component.ts) is correct.
- VUE out-tf-vue/web/src/pages/mixed.vue — compiles but is silently WRONG: only `const create = reactive(useCreateItem())` + `const form = useLoomForm(CreateItemRequest, { name: "" })` are declared; the Note <v-form> binds `v-model="form.values.text"` and submits `create.mutateAsync(vals)` (the Item mutation, Item schema) — `useCreateNote`/`CreateNoteRequest` are never imported at all. Submitting the Note form posts Item data to /items.
- feliz (out-tf-feliz/web/src/App.fs:115-157) and flutter (out-tf-flutter/web/lib/pages/home_page.dart) are correct.

open.repro: scratchpad/fe-combos/twoforms.ddd + tf-{react,vue,svelte,angular,feliz,flutter}.ddd
open.impact: Any page with two create forms (a very ordinary shape — e.g. a dashboard offering 'new customer' and 'new order') fails to build on react/svelte/angular, and on vue silently POSTs the wrong aggregate to the wrong endpoint. No shipped fixture has two CreateForms on one page, so no gate sees it.
open.fix: Name the per-form shell locals after the form (aggregate + testid namespace) the way Angular already does cross-aggregate, and dedupe by that key instead of by aggregate; on Vue key the recorded FormOfState by form identity so a second form gets its own `create`/`form` + imports.

reconciled.evidence: regenerated: wreact/src/pages/home.tsx (`const create` + the useForm destructure emitted TWICE in one function scope), wsv/src/routes/(app)/mixed/+page.svelte:8-11 (same, cross-aggregate), wng/src/app/pages/home.component.ts:28-37 (`itemCreate`/`itemForm`/`onSubmitItem` declared twice -> TS2300 x3), wvue/src/pages/mixed.vue (only useCreateItem imported; the Note form binds form.values.text and submits the Item mutation)
reconciled.note: All four arms reproduce unchanged: react/svelte/angular fail to build, vue compiles but silently POSTs Item data for the Note form; Angular's cross-aggregate mixed.component.ts is correct, so only the same-aggregate path collides there. [Contamination check: bin/cli.js probe RE-RUN 2026-08-31 05:53 UTC against the post-05:42 rebuild (`npx tsc -b` clean, no-op); output byte-identical, verdict unchanged.]

open.title: `For` as the direct body of a `QueryView { data: }` lambda emits syntactically invalid source on React (object literal), Feliz (`yield!` outside a seq) and Flutter (spread in expression position)
open.repro: scratchpad/fe-combos/for1.ddd + for1-{vue,svelte,angular,feliz,flutter}.ddd
open.impact: The simplest hand-written list page (`QueryView { of: X.all, data: rows => For { each: rows, ... } }`) produces a project that does not parse on 3 of 6 frontends. Wrapping the For in a `Stack` happens to hide it, which is why no example caught it.
open.fix: Have emitQueryView wrap a lambda body whose top node is a children-position primitive in the target's fragment/children wrapper (the `wrapMultiRoot` seam already exists for the Table-filter case), or make renderForEach's emptyBody-less arm return a self-contained expression on these three targets.

reconciled.evidence: regenerated from `QueryView { of: S.Item.all, data: rows => For { each: rows, r => Text { r.name } } }`: wreact/src/pages/p1.tsx (a `{...map(...)}` brace block in expression position after `&& (`), wfz/src/App.fs:81 (bare `yield!` inside a lambda body, not a seq), wfl/lib/pages/p1_page.dart:14 (`... spread` in expression position)

open.title: The `auto-paged-table` macro rewrites only the Table's own `rows:` slot, leaving every SIBLING reader of the same QueryView binding pointed at the paged envelope

evidence.text:
Minimal pair in ONE generated app (fixture for2.ddd; the two pages differ only by a sibling Table):
- page A1 `data: rows => Stack { For { each: rows, r => Text { r.name } } }` → out-for2/web/src/pages/a1.tsx:21 `{itemAll.data.items.map((r, rIdx) => (` — CORRECT.
- page A2 `data: rows => Stack { For { each: rows, ... }, Table { Column {...}, rows: rows } }` → out-for2/web/src/pages/a2.tsx:25 `{itemAll.data.map((r, rIdx) => (` (WRONG — the envelope) and :37 `itemAll.data.items.map((row) => (` (the Table compensating).
`itemAll.data` is typed `ItemPaged = z.object({ items, page, pageSize, total, totalPages })` (out-for2/web/src/api/item.ts:35) → `.map` is TS2339 + a runtime TypeError.
Same shape on every other target (fixture lam.ddd): vue out-lam-vue/web/src/pages/p.vue:31 `v-for="(r, rIdx) in itemAll.data"` (iterates the envelope's VALUES); svelte out-lam-svelte/.../p/+page.svelte:20 `{#each itemAll.data as r}`; angular out-lam-angular/.../p.component.ts:25 `@for (r of itemAll.data()!; track $index)` → NG02200; flutter out-lam-flutter/web/lib/pages/p_page.dart:55 `itemAll.map(...)` on an `ItemPaged` → Dart compile error. Feliz is unaffected (its wire decodes only `items`).
ROOT: src/macros/stdlib/auto-paged-table.ts — the macro flips the QueryView to `paged: true` (binding stays the envelope) and rewrites the Table to `rows: rows.items`, but nothing rewrites the other uses of the lambda binding in the same body.

open.repro: scratchpad/fe-combos/for2.ddd (pages A1 vs A2); scratchpad/fe-combos/lam.ddd for the cross-target set
open.impact: Adding an ordinary Table next to a For inside one QueryView silently re-points the For at `{items, page, ...}` — a TypeScript error plus a render-time crash on 4 frontends and a Dart compile error on Flutter, with no diagnostic. The author never wrote the rewrite that broke it.
open.fix: In auto-paged-table.ts, when the QueryView is upgraded to `paged: true`, rewrite EVERY reference to the data-lambda binding in that lambda (not just the Table's `rows:`) to `<binding>.items`, except the envelope members the pager reads (`.totalPages`, `.total`, `.page`).

reconciled.evidence: src/macros/stdlib/auto-paged-table.ts:250-300 (repointBindingReaders) + ENVELOPE_MEMBERS at :228; test/macro/auto-paged-table.test.ts:164, :181, :196
reconciled.note: Re-verified by generating the exact minimal pair: the sibling `For { each: rows }` now emits `itemAll.data.items.map((r, rIdx) => …)` (was `itemAll.data.map`), the pager's `rows.totalPages` is left as written, and a chained `rows.count()` is re-pointed through `.items`.

Complete elixir's coerceOpParam over int/bool (its own docstring documents the failure mode). Runtime-verify the Java 1.5→int truncation and pin strict rejection. Record the stringified-number acceptance skew and pin a decision (lax everywhere or strict everywhere). Tests: a cross-backend ingress conformance matrix (bad money string, fractional int, stringified number, huge money) asserting 4xx per backend; mutation-prove one arm per backend. open.title: `lineage` is declared a non-nullable object in `.loom/wire-spec.json` and in elixir's OpenApiSpex schema, while every backend puts `"lineage": null` on the wire

evidence.text:
src/ir/stdlib/generics.ts:95 declares the carrier member as `{ name: PROVENANCE_LINEAGE_FIELD, type: jsonType, optional: true }` — OPTIONAL, with no nullability. Optionality and nullability are different claims, and the emitters pick different halves:
  .loom/wire-spec.json (phase ⑨): `"total": { "type":"object", "properties": { "value": {"type":"integer"}, "lineage": {"type":"object"} }, "required": ["value"], "additionalProperties": false }`
  elixir  d/lib/d_web/api/schemas/order_response.ex:16 `total: %Schema{type: :object, properties: %{value: …, lineage: %Schema{type: :object}}, required: [:value]}`
  node    d/http/order.routes.ts:58 `total: z.object({ value: z.number().int(), lineage: ProvenanceLineage.nullable() })`   ← required + NULLABLE
  python  d/app/http/wire_models.py:25 `lineage: dict[str, object] | None = None`                                    ← optional + nullable
  react/vue/svelte  src/api/order.ts:54 `lineage: provLineageSchema.nullish()`                                    ← optional + nullable
And the value actually produced is an explicit null, present in the body: node repository `lineage: root.total_provenance ?? null`; python `"lineage": (root.total_provenance.to_wire() if … else None)`; elixir `"lineage" => record.total_provenance` over a nullable jsonb column; dotnet `Provenanced<T>(T Value, ProvLineage? Lineage)` and java `record Provenanced<T>(T value, ProvLineage lineage)` with no NON_NULL/WhenWritingNull configured anywhere in the emitted projects (grepped).

open.repro: generate corpus/provenance.ddd (or any `T provenanced` aggregate) on node + elixir; read `.loom/wire-spec.json` aggregates.Order.properties.total and `d/lib/d_web/api/schemas/order_response.ex`, then compare against d/http/order.routes.ts:58. Runtime confirmation needs a boot + a GET on a row created before any provenanced write — that is the one step I could not run here, hence `likely` not `proven`.
open.impact: For any row whose provenanced field has never been written, the emitted body carries `"lineage": null` — which validates against node's and python's published schemas and VIOLATES elixir's `%Schema{type: :object}` and the shared `.loom/wire-spec.json` (JSON Schema applies the subschema whenever the key is present; `required` does not save it). A contract-diff over wire-spec.json, or a schemathesis/OpenAPI-conformance run against the Phoenix app, should flag the app's own response as non-conforming. Four different nullability declarations of ONE member is also the drift `src/util/provenance-carrier.ts` was created to prevent — it centralised the NAMES but not the nullability.
open.fix: Give `GENERIC_SHAPES.provenanced`'s lineage member an explicit nullable marker and have wire-spec.ts and the elixir OpenApiSpex emitter render `nullable: true` / `anyOf [object, null]` from it — one declaration, five consumers, same as the member names.

reconciled.evidence: src/ir/stdlib/generics.ts:94 (`{ name: PROVENANCE_LINEAGE_FIELD, type: jsonType, optional: true }` — optional, never nullable); reproduced on corpus/provenance.ddd: .loom/wire-spec.json `total.properties.lineage = {"type":"object"}` with `required:["value"]`, elixir d/lib/d_web/api/schemas/order_response.ex:16 the same, vs node d/http/order.routes.ts:58 `lineage: ProvenanceLineage.nullable()`
reconciled.note: Declaration half re-proved on disk: the wire-spec and the elixir OpenApiSpex schema both declare a non-nullable object for a field every backend ships as an explicit null; #2687's elixir openapi work does not touch it.

open.title: Validator falsely rejects `money * <numeric literal>` and `money / <numeric literal>` — with a message that says the form is allowed

evidence.text:
src/language/validators/types.ts:390-397 applies literal promotion BEFORE the arithmetic check: `literalPromotionAnchor(money)` returns "money" (src/language/validators/_shared.ts:193-197), so `canPromoteAstLitTo(2, "money")` rewrites the int literal's type to `money`, turning `money × int` into `money × money`, which `moneyArithmetic` (src/language/type-system.ts:742-765) rejects — and the failure branch at types.ts:435-445 then prints the money hint verbatim.
TRANSCRIPT (`node bin/cli.js parse /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/lit.ddd`), fixture has `derived a: money = discount * 2` / `derived c: money = discount / 2`:
  lit.ddd:7:39 error: Operator '*' has incompatible operand types: left is 'money', right is 'money'. Allowed for money: money ± money, money × {int|long|decimal}, money ÷ {int|long|decimal}.
  lit.ddd:9:39 error: Operator '/' has incompatible operand types: left is 'money', right is 'money'. Allowed for money: money ± money, money × {int|long|decimal}, money ÷ {int|long|decimal}.
Characterised: `discount * n` (int VARIABLE) passes; `discount + 1` passes (money ± money is legal); `discount * 2.5` also fails; `discount * decimal(2)` (explicit convert, not a literal) passes.

open.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/lit.ddd and lit2.ddd; `node bin/cli.js parse`.
open.impact: `derived half: money = price / 2` and `total * 2` — about as basic as money arithmetic gets — are unwritable, and the diagnostic contradicts itself, so the author has no path to the workaround (`price / decimal(2)`). Note the lowering carries the same promotion (`literalPromotionAnchor` at src/ir/lower/lower-expr.ts:2092-2110), so simply relaxing the validator would push a `money × money` IR node into the renderers — both halves need the fix.
open.fix: Don't promote a numeric literal to `money` when the operator is `*` or `/` (money scaling is by a SCALAR, not by money); leave promotion in place for `+`/`-` and comparisons. Same edit in validators/types.ts:390-397 and lower-expr.ts's promotion. Mutation-prove: seed `derived a: money = discount * 2` and check it both parses and emits `times(2)` / `.multiply(...)` / `Decimal.mult(...)`.
related_to: fleet1 G2644-M-T6.44 (claimed by #2670) fixes the RENDER leaves; this is the AST validator half

reconciled.evidence: src/language/validators/types.ts:391-397 still applies literalPromotionAnchor BEFORE the arithmetic check; REPRODUCED: `derived a: money = discount * 2`, `= discount / 2`, `= discount * 2.5` all rejected as "left is 'money', right is 'money'" by a message that lists money × {int|long|decimal} as allowed
reconciled.note: #2670 (merged) fixed the RENDER leaves only; the AST-validator half (and the mirrored promotion in lower-expr.ts) is untouched — `discount * n` with an int VARIABLE still passes, so it is literal-only.

open.title: String literals inside a `match` in a user-visible slot are silently untranslatable, while string `+` in the SAME slot is a hard validator error — `ddd i18n check --strict` passes on a page shipping hardcoded English

evidence.text:
SHIPPED example, not a synthetic one: web/src/examples/expression-showcase.ddd:231 `Stat { "match", match { count > 5 => "many", count > 1 => "some", else => "none" } }`.
Generated (out-expr/web_app/src/pages/kinds.tsx:36-37):
  <Text size="sm" c="dimmed">{t("page.Kinds.statLabel.yzu1sm", "match")}</Text>
  <Text fw={700} size="xl">{((count > 5) ? "many" : ((count > 1) ? "some" : "none"))}</Text>
The label (positional 0 of the same `Stat`) is t()-wrapped; the arms are raw. grep for many/some/none in out-expr/.loom/messages.en.json → absent.
Same in the combo fixture: out-react/web_app/src/pages/board_page.tsx:56 `? "Live now" : (... ? "Still a draft" : "Archived away")` — none of the three is in out-react/.loom/messages.en.json (which does carry every sibling slot literal).
ROOT + the asymmetry: src/util/user-visible-slots.ts extracts only when the slot value is a bare literal ("a non-literal slot is simply skipped by both consumers", header comment), while the OTHER consumer of the same table — `loom.user-visible-concat` (src/language/validators/i18n-strings.ts) — makes string `+` in that identical slot an ERROR precisely because "concatenation can't be translated". A `match` producing literals is exactly as untranslatable and is accepted in silence.

open.repro: node bin/cli.js generate system web/src/examples/expression-showcase.ddd -o out-expr; diff out-expr/web_app/src/pages/kinds.tsx against out-expr/.loom/messages.en.json
open.impact: Authors are pushed off `+` by an error and onto `match`/ternary, which then ships permanently-English text through the strict CI i18n gate. Affects every frontend, since the raw literal is emitted by the shared expression path.
open.fix: Either extract match/ternary arms that are string literals inside a user-visible slot into the catalog (they have a stable role+hash the same way the direct literal does), or extend `loom.user-visible-concat` to reject a non-extractable literal-bearing expression in those slots so the gap is honest.

reconciled.evidence: src/language/validators/i18n-strings.ts:63-82 checkUserVisibleConcat rejects only a `+` chain (stringConcat at :40) and skips every other non-literal slot; src/generator/_walker/i18n-extract.ts:54 literalString returns undefined for a match/ternary, so its arms are never catalogued
reconciled.note: The asymmetry stands: `+` in a user-visible slot is a hard error, a `match` producing the same literals ships raw English past `ddd i18n check --strict` (shipped example web/src/examples/expression-showcase.ddd:231).

Elixir's `first` and `firstOrNull` are literally the SAME snippet (:882 vs :883), so the non-optional form silently degrades. src/util/collection-ops.ts:23 declares `first` as returning `T` (non-optional) and the cross-backend semantics contract in src/util/intrinsics.ts pins edge behaviour for every scalar intrinsic but says nothing about `first`.
EMITTED (node) /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Loc/51e0d493-39ca-59a9-9783-d320c97c6f95/scratchpad/expr/out-node/d/domain/order.ts:120 — `get firstSku(): string { return (this._lines)[0].sku; }` — a `string`-typed getter that throws on an empty collection but returns `undefined` for a bare `lines.first`.

open.impact: The same .ddd yields a 500 on java/.NET/python and a null/undefined that flows onto the wire (or a later NPE-equivalent) on node/elixir. A behavioral wire-golden captured on one backend cannot be trusted for another.
open.fix: Pin the contract in src/util/collection-ops.ts the way src/util/intrinsics.ts pins scalar edge behaviour (either "throws" everywhere or "first is optional"), then align the five leaves and add a per-backend arm test. If "throws" wins, elixir needs `hd/1` and node an explicit guard.

reconciled.evidence: src/generator/dotnet/render-expr.ts:902 `first: (recv) => \`${recv}.First()\`` vs typescript/render-expr.ts:416 `${recv}[0]`, java:700 `.get(0)`, python:589 `[0]`, elixir:883 `List.first(${recv})`

open.title: A `valueobject` aggregate field publishes ONE shared component on node/python/elixir and TWO (`<VO>Request` + `<VO>Response`) on dotnet/java

evidence.text: out-node/d/http/widget.routes.ts:14-19 `const DimensionsSchema = z.object({…}).openapi("Dimensions")` used by BOTH the request and the response schemas; out-elixir/d/lib/d_web/api/schemas/dimensions.ex is likewise the single `Dimensions` component (WidgetResponse refs `#/components/schemas/Dimensions`); out-python/d/app/http/widget_routes.py:21 `from app.http.wire_models import Dimensions as DimensionsModel` (one model). Against: out-dotnet/d/Application/Widgets/Requests/WidgetRequests.cs:11 `record DimensionsRequest(…)` + Responses/WidgetResponses.cs:10 `record DimensionsResponse(…)`; out-java/…/features/widgets/DimensionsRequest.java and DimensionsResponse.java. The `dims` property therefore carries `$ref: Dimensions` on three backends and `$ref: DimensionsRequest`/`DimensionsResponse` on two — a `propertyTypes` (`ref:<Name>`) and a `schemaNames` divergence.

open.repro: aggregate field `dims: Dimensions`; generate all five and diff `components.schemas` names + the `dims` property `$ref`. Fixture: scratchpad/wirediff/rich2.tmpl.ddd
open.impact: Generated clients get different type names and a different type count for the same DSL construct; a spec-diff consumer sees two components appear/disappear per backend. Un-gated because examples/showcase.ddd declares `valueobject Slug` and `valueobject Duration` but never uses either as an aggregate field (grep for `: Slug` / `: Duration` returns nothing), so the strict parity job never compares a VO. java additionally has no `RequiredSet` entry for `DimensionsResponse` in OpenApiContractCustomizer, so its required set is empty where elixir declares `[width, height]`.

In-window rewrite: src/ir/validate/checks/store-checks.ts deleted `LIFETIME_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORMS` and replaced the platform-wide arm with two per-field blocks — :312-338 (feliz, `if (felizPersistCodec(f.type)) continue`, message key `loom.store-lifetime-target-unsupported#field`) and :340-361 (flutter, `flutterPersistCodec`, key `#flutter-field`). So `persist: local` over a `datetime` or `enum` field ships on flutter and is REFUSED on feliz; over a `json` field it ships on feliz and is REFUSED on flutter. Register row src/diagnostics/unsupported-register.ts:288-294 (kind `gap`, mission M-T1.20) was reworded for this in-window but still names one code for two different boundaries.

[ALSO REPORTED BY t1-frontend as `M-T1.20-store-lifetime-field-residue` (kind=honest, size=M)]: src/ir/validate/checks/store-checks.ts:20 records that `LIFETIME_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORMS` had its last entry removed; the code now fires only through the `#field` / `#flutter-field` message variants for a cell type with no total F#/Dart conversion. Feliz needs `System.DateTime.TryParse` / `System.Guid.TryParse` arms and an enum arm (parse by case name, fall back to the default case — total by construction, matching the JS decoders); Flutter needs a `json` arm (store the raw JSON string, restore as `dynamic`). Pin with a matrix test over the two tables asserting set equality except for the entries carrying a written reason.

open.title: #2644 F13 / M-T5.23 — `long` has no contract: JS-number storage and float() aggregates corrupt past 2^53; int-overflow is 3-way divergent

evidence.text: Documented by register-only PR #2644 (F13, CONFIRMED): node stores long as a JS number (`bigint(col, {mode:"number"})` in src/generator/typescript/emit/schema.ts; mikroorm `ts: "number"`) and python's aggregate arm goes through `float()` — silent corruption past 2^53 — while .NET/Java/Elixir carry int64 exactly. Aggregate int-overflow is three-way divergent: Java `((Number) x).intValue()` wraps silently, .NET's `(int)` cast from decimal throws (500), the rest pass the too-big value through. No validator, no doc caveat. Annex: python ships declared-int aggregates through float() and relies on pydantic lax-mode re-coercion — one strict-mode flip from a 500.

out-node/d/db/schema.ts:13 `serial: bigint("serial", { mode: "number" }).notNull()` (drizzle hands back a JS number), out-node/d/http/widget.routes.ts:24 request `serial: z.number().int()` and :88 response `serial: z.number().int()`, out-node/d/domain/widget.ts constructor `serial: number`. The other four keep 64-bit types: out-java Widget.java `long serial`, out-dotnet WidgetResponses.cs `[property: Required] long Serial`, out-python `serial: int` (arbitrary precision), out-elixir `field :serial, :integer` over `add :serial, :bigint`. The wire-spec (identical on all five) declares `serial: {type: integer}` with no bound.

open.repro: aggregate field `serial: long`; POST 9007199254740993 and GET it back on node vs java. Fixture: scratchpad/wirediff/rich2.tmpl.ddd
open.impact: `POST {"serial": 9007199254740993}` is accepted by every backend's declared contract but silently becomes 9007199254740992 on node — stored and echoed wrong — while the other four persist it exactly. Same family as the waived schemathesis F11 (`int` published with no bound over an int4 column) but on the READ side and for `long`, and schemathesis only runs the node leg so nothing else can see it.
open.fix: Proposed default (overridable): document + validator-enforce a 2^53 safe-integer ceiling for long on the affected paths NOW (an honest loom.* diagnostic, not silent corruption); a BigInt/string-wire representation upgrade becomes a named follow-up if the ceiling pinches. Route python declared int/long aggregates through int(), not float(). Unify aggregate-overflow behaviour across the three. Tests: validator tests, a >2^53 witness on the exact backends proving THEY carry it, a python aggregate int test.

open.title: The mikroorm half of the self-provisioning-adapter gate rationale is factually wrong on today's emitter (`safe: true`)

evidence.text: src/ir/validate/checks/migration-checks.ts:182-185 states: 'mikroorm: `updateSchema()` has no rename intent to consult, so it sees a dropped column and an added one — it DROPS the old column and ADDS the new one, i.e. it deletes the very data the rename existed to keep.' The gate itself is still correct to exist; only its stated rationale — the thing a reader uses to decide urgency — is wrong.

open.title: 36 of 46 `*-unsupported` register rows cite a stale `file:line` emission site; the gate only checks the string SHAPE

evidence.text:
Ran on this checkout: for each of the 46 `UNSUPPORTED_REGISTER` rows, read `site` and check whether the row's `code` appears within ±5 lines of the cited line. 36 miss. Examples in this bucket: `loom.workflow-load-array-unsupported` cites `src/ir/validate/checks/workflow-checks.ts:591`, actual emission is :643; `loom.workflow-load-nullable-unsupported` cites :600, actual :656; `loom.saving-shape-unsupported` cites `system-checks.ts:1282`, actual :1642; `loom.vanilla-document-unsupported` cites :1528, actual is the pass beginning :1659. The test only validates the FORMAT — test/system/unsupported-register.test.ts:131-135 `it("cites a site for every row")` asserts `/^src\/.+:\d+$/` and nothing more. The `site` field's stated purpose is 'file:line of the first emission site, FOR THE REVIEWER' (unsupported-register.ts:57), which is exactly what rots. #2667 edits this file but is register-only.

[ALSO REPORTED BY t6-backend as `register-site-lines-unverified` (kind=stale-prose, size=S)]: test/system/unsupported-register.test.ts:131-136 asserts only `/^src\/.+:\d+$/`. Sampled three rows against main and all three miss: `loom.mikroorm-unsupported` cites system-checks.ts:2456 (a filter-bypass comment block, :2454-2458); `loom.audited-backend-unsupported` cites :3484 (the line is `const EVENT_SOURCING_BACKENDS = …`, :3482-3484); `loom.context-filter-unsupported` cites :1998 (a `walkExpr` switch arm, :1996-2000). The file's own header comment (unsupported-register.ts, and M-T6.34's Sources line in T6) already warns "cited by SYMBOL, not line: this file's own citations went stale the moment the cited file was edited" — the register did not take its own advice.

open.fix:
Replace the format assertion in test/system/unsupported-register.test.ts:131-135 with a real one: read the cited file, assert `row.code` occurs within a small window of `site`'s line (a ±5-line window is enough to survive formatting churn), and fail with the corrected line number so the fix is mechanical. Then run it once and rewrite the 36 stale sites. This turns `site` into a pinned fact rather than a comment — the same ratchet discipline CLAUDE.md requires of waivers.

[ALTERNATE FIX RECIPE from t6-backend/register-site-lines-unverified]: Either cite the SYMBOL (`system-checks.ts:validateAuditedOperationSupport`) and have the gate resolve it, or keep line numbers and make the gate assert the cited file:line actually matches the row's `code:` literal. The second is the mutation-provable one: move any row's line by ±2 and it must go red.
